page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.3xlarge is a high-clock-speed computing instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 12 vCPUs distributed across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration includes 48.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is rated at a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware instruction flags include broad SIMD support with AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration and bit-manipulation extensions. In synthetic benchmark runs, the instance demonstrates mid-tier, consistent performance across standard workloads. Stress-ng records a single-core score of 1574.38 and a multi-core score of 12320.1. Geekbench measures 1267.0 in single-core and 6488.0 in multi-core metrics, achieving 10661.0 on Clang software compilation and 9582.0 on ray tracing tasks. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 62.11 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 33.39 GB/sec write throughput.

Without dedicated GPU accelerators, the instance shows distinct limits on machine learning inferencing. While small 135M parameter language models achieve 752.4 prompt tokens per second and 155.04 generation tokens per second, execution on 7B models drops significantly to 17.49 prompt tokens per second and 7.5 generation tokens per second. In transactional and web testing, the platform delivered 11.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.92 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, dedicated 3.3 GHz core clock rate, and lack of onboard storage, ecs.hfg7.3xlarge functions effectively as a balanced compute engine. It is well configured for continuous integration pipelines, software build clusters, web application backends, and in-memory caches or enterprise database engines relying on external block storage.
